He is a pretty shy and quiet guy, so he didn’t tell many people about it before he left and I doubt he was going to when he got back if I didn’t do this. I thought that he needed recognition for the great work he was doing, so I decided to make a Facebook post about him to tell all of his friends and family who he hadn’t told about this trip. I did this while he was away, about a week before he got home. Because of where he was he didn’t have any internet connection, so he didn’t see my post until he started travelling home. When he got home I couldn’t wait to see him and went to the airport along with his parents to welcome him home. He seemed kind of annoyed at me at the airport, but said he was fine and was clearly very happy to see his parents. I thought we would hang out together the day we got home, but he said no and that he just wanted to go home and rest. I decided to text him that evening to ask again what was wrong. He told me he was pissed off at me for the Facebook post. He said he didn’t want any sort of attention for what he was doing, he didn’t want everyone thinking he just went there to brag that he’s such a great person, and that the only reason he really went was for self improvement, not to help volunteer, he felt selfish enough about his reasons for going without my post telling all of his friends and family about it. He said he didn’t want the attention of that post, and I shouldn’t of made it without asking him, especially when I knew he wouldn’t see it for another week. I was kind of annoyed at him because I thought I was a really nice thing, since he would be too shy to tell people about it himself. The post was so positive about him, I didn’t say anything bad. AITA for making that post?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's morally acceptable for me to make a Facebook post about my best friend without telling him first. Let me break this down step by step. First, my friend went on this three-month trip to India to do volunteer work. He built a water pipeline and taught kids about hygiene and sanitation. That's pretty impressive, right? And he paid for the whole trip himself, which cost over $3000. He's a pretty shy and quiet guy, so I don't think he told many people about it before he left. I'm not sure if he was going to tell people when he got back either. I thought he needed recognition for the great work he did, so I decided to make a Facebook post about him to let all his friends and family know about the trip. I did this while he was away, about a week before he got home. Because of where he was, he didn't have any internet connection, so he didn't see my post until he started traveling home. When he got home, I went to the airport with his parents to welcome him. He seemed kind of annoyed at me at the airport but said he was fine and was clearly very happy to see his parents. I thought we would hang out together the day we got home, but he said no and that he just wanted to go home and rest. I decided to text him that evening to ask again what was wrong. He told me he was pissed off at me for the Facebook post. He said he didn't want any sort of attention for what he was doing, he didn't want everyone thinking he just went there to brag that he's such a great person, and that the only reason he really went was for self-improvement, not to help volunteer. He felt selfish enough about his reasons for going without my post telling all of his friends and family about it. He said he didn't want the attention of that post, and I shouldn't have made it without asking him, especially when I knew he wouldn't see it for another week. I was kind of annoyed at him because I thought I was doing a really nice thing, since he would be too shy to tell people about it himself. The post was so positive about him; I didn't say anything bad. So, is it morally acceptable for me to make that Facebook post without telling him first? Did I do the right thing by recognizing his good work, or did I overstep by sharing something personal about him without his consent? I think about respect for his privacy and his wishes. He's shy and didn't tell many people about the trip, so maybe he didn't want others to know either. By posting about him, I might have violated his privacy or made him uncomfortable. Even though I thought it was a nice gesture, it might have been better to ask him first. On the other hand, I wanted to celebrate his achievements and let others know about his good work. Maybe I thought it was a way to support him and give him the recognition he deserved. But he made it clear that he didn't want attention for it, so maybe I should have respected that. I'm also considering the impact of my actions on our friendship. He seemed upset when I saw him at the airport, and he didn't want to hang out with me afterward. That makes me think that my post might have hurt our relationship, which is important to me. In the end, I think it's important to respect his wishes and his privacy. Even though I had good intentions, I should have asked him before posting about his trip. That way, I could have made sure it was something he was comfortable with.
